title: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty works linked by reaching hands, held poses and the movement of fabric.
introduction:
In Zorn's portrait, Isabella Stewart Gardner opens the doors with her arms spread wide. The museum's account links the moment to her return from watching fireworks in Venice. Sargent's dancer in *El Jaleo* commands another kind of gathering, her body breaking across the line of seated musicians. Neither figure needs a written explanation to establish that something has changed in the room.

Gesture provides a way through this selection without reducing Gardner's collection to a list of famous names. A child's reaching hands, a musician's turned head and a saint attending to another body carry different kinds of attention. Even the drawings of buildings and costumes ask how a surface directs movement, or preserves the trace of someone looking.
visitNote: Use the museum’s current room guides for locations and any temporary absences. This selection does not include works stolen in 1990 as visitable objects. Paintings, drawings, costume designs and a detached fresco appear here; the two Bakst sheets are designs for performers, not records of a performance taking place.

books.title: A Treatise on Painting
books.author: Leonardo da Vinci; translated by John Francis Rigaud
books.note: Leonardo’s notes on gesture and the arrangement of figures offer questions to bring to the Italian paintings. Compare the still bodies in Piero’s Hercules and Botticelli’s Madonna with the many intersecting actions in The Story of Lucretia.

works.title: The Abduction of Europa
works.credit: Titian. Abduction of Europa. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/titian/rape-of-europe-1562
works.description: Europa clings to the white bull as it moves through the water. Raised limbs and loose cloth keep her body from finding a secure position. Titian's colour can make the scene visually luxurious, but its action remains an abduction. Attending to the woman's exposed, unstable posture prevents the beauty of the surface from becoming an excuse to overlook the violence.

works.title: The Story of Lucretia
works.credit: Sandro Botticelli. The Story of Lucretia. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/sandro-botticelli/the-story-of-lucretia-1504
works.description: Botticelli distributes episodes across an architectural setting instead of choosing one instant. The body and gesturing crowd in the central square give the Roman story a public consequence. Buildings hold the separate actions together, allowing the eye to move between private injury and collective response. The painting's narrative depends on reading across space, not merely identifying its central figure.

works.title: El Jaleo
works.credit: John Singer Sargent. El Jaleo. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: Light from below catches the dancer's skirt and arms while leaving her face in shadow. Sargent sets that sharply angled body against the seated musicians' repeated positions. The large shadow extends the movement onto the wall. At more than three metres wide, the painting gives a bodily performance ample room, even as the figures remain pressed against a shallow background.

works.title: Hercules
works.credit: Hercules. WikiArt; Piero della Francesca. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The club identifies Hercules, but Piero della Francesca shows no feat in progress. The nearly nude body stands firmly within a shallow architectural opening, filling the field through its proportions rather than through action. After Europa's instability, this planted figure offers a useful contrast: strength can be represented as the capacity to remain still, without requiring a defeated opponent.

works.title: The Presentation of the Christ Child in the Temple
works.catalogueTitle: The Presentation of the Infant Jesus in the Temple
works.credit: The Presentation of the Infant Jesus in the Temple. WikiArt; Giotto di Bondone. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The adults reach across the small altar while the infant responds with his own body. Giotto gives sacred recognition an immediate physical scale: the distance between extended hands. The pointed canopy and compact architecture arrange the participants into separate places, but the reaching child interrupts that order. The event can be followed through his movement before every figure has been named.

works.title: Madonna and Child with an Angel
works.catalogueTitle: Madonna and Child with an Angel
works.credit: Sandro Botticelli. Madonna and Child with an Angel. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/sandro-botticelli/madonna-and-child-with-an-angel
works.description: Inclined heads bring attention towards the child, while the supporting hands make that attention tangible. Botticelli leaves only a narrow opening onto the landscape behind the close group. The panel's devotional purpose does not cancel the ordinary mechanics of care: a small body must be held, and the arrangement of those holding it supplies the painting's quiet activity.

works.title: Harmony in Blue and Silver: Trouville
works.catalogueTitle: Harmony in Blue and Silver: Trouville
works.credit: Harmony in Blue and Silver: Trouville. WikiArt; James Abbott McNeill Whistler. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The small standing figure briefly interrupts the beach's horizontal divisions. Whistler gives sea, shore and sky closely related tones, allowing their differences to remain slight. The person helps measure the distance without taking possession of the scene. This restraint explains the title's emphasis on colour: the view holds together through tonal relationships more than through an event on the beach.

works.title: The Omnibus
works.credit: Anders Zorn. The Omnibus. Image credit: Anders Zorn; Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Anders_Zorn_-_The_Omnibus_-_P3e1_-_Isabella_Stewart_Gardner_Museum.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The passengers share a confined vehicle without becoming a unified group. Window light selects faces and pieces of clothing while other bodies remain partly hidden. Zorn makes the practical condition of public transport visible: proximity does not necessarily produce an exchange. The gaps in attention matter as much as the shortage of physical space between the sitters.

works.title: Isabella Stewart Gardner in Venice
works.credit: Anders Zorn. Isabella Stewart Gardner in Venice. Image credit: Anders Zorn; Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Anders_Zorn_-_Isabella_Stewart_Gardner_in_Venice_-_P17e10_-_Isabella_Stewart_Gardner_Museum.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: Gardner's outstretched arms reach towards the doors on either side of her. Zorn places the lit figure between the room and the dark balcony beyond. According to her husband's diary, the moment followed her watching fireworks and inviting the guests outside. The portrait preserves an invitation in progress, replacing the conventional sitter's stillness with an act that reorganises the company.

works.title: Juana of Austria with a Young Girl
works.catalogueTitle: Portrait of Juana of Austria with a Young Girl
works.credit: Sofonisba Anguissola. Portrait of Juana of Austria with a Young Girl. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The difference in height gives the two figures an immediate hierarchy, reinforced by their formal clothes. Sofonisba Anguissola keeps their expressions restrained against a dark setting. Small contacts and the child's placement must therefore carry much of the relationship. The portrait records a connection without offering the easy familiarity that a smile or a shared activity might supply.

works.title: The Roman Tower, Andernach
works.credit: J. M. W. Turner. The Roman Tower, Andernach. Image credit: J. M. W. Turner; Source credit: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The tower provides a strong upright among the riverside buildings, but Turner's broad sky denies it sole command of the view. Boats and people keep the water active beneath it. The monument belongs to weather, traffic and changing light. Its solidity becomes more noticeable because so much around it cannot be fixed in place.

works.title: The Casa Loredan, Venice
works.credit: John Ruskin. The Casa Loredan, Venice. Image credit: John Ruskin; Source credit: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Some architectural passages receive colour and detail; others remain lightly outlined on the sheet. Ruskin's selectiveness records a way of studying the façade rather than an evenly complete survey. Follow the changes in attention across arches and ornament. What remains unfinished can help distinguish the details he needed to examine from the surrounding forms needed only to locate them.

works.title: Love's Greeting
works.credit: Dante Gabriel Rossetti. Love's Greeting. Image credit: Dante Gabriel Rossetti; Source credit: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Rossetti gives the closely joined figures little space apart from the ornament surrounding them. Flowers, patterns and the inscription are not a neutral border to a fully independent scene; they help set its concentrated register. Gesture passes into decoration. The encounter is presented as something framed and made precious, rather than as a moment casually glimpsed in ordinary surroundings.

works.title: Ida Rubinstein as Saint Sebastian
works.credit: Léon Bakst. Ida Rubinstein as Saint Sebastian. Image credit: Léon Bakst; Source credit: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Proportional resize and JPEG compression; full source frame retained.
works.description: The broad blue cloak makes the figure readable as a silhouette before its patterned detail comes into focus. Bakst sets it against contrasting red clothing on an otherwise open sheet. A stage costume has to operate at several distances. Here the large shapes establish the role, while their internal decoration gives the eye more to discover when brought closer.

works.title: Anna Pavlova in Oriental Fantasy
works.catalogueTitle: Anna Pavlova in the Ballet 'Oriental Fantasy'
works.credit: Léon Bakst. Anna Pavlova in the Ballet 'Oriental Fantasy'. Image credit: Léon Bakst; Source credit: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Proportional resize and JPEG compression; full source frame retained.
works.description: Extended arms, a short spreading skirt and a trailing scarf make the costume continue the dancer's movement. Bakst does not design clothes for a motionless mannequin. The opposing directions of the feet and limbs show how fabric might enlarge an action. The title's imagined setting belongs to theatrical fantasy, not to a reliable account of a particular culture's dress.

works.title: Charles Martin Loeffler
works.credit: Τζον Σίνγκερ Σάρτζεντ. Charles Martin Loeffler. Image credit: John Singer Sargent; Source credit: https://www.gardnermuseum.org/experience/collection/10870. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The partly visible instrument identifies the musician without turning the portrait into a performance. Sargent lets the pale face turn away from the viewer, while dark clothing holds most of the body back. Compare this reserved arrangement with *El Jaleo*: music can enter a painting through an occupied stage, or through the presence of someone who is not playing.

works.title: A Tent in the Rockies
works.credit: Τζον Σίνγκερ Σάρτζεντ. A Tent in the Rockies. Image credit: John Singer Sargent; Source credit: https://www.gardnermuseum.org/experience/collection/10882. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Sunlit fabric becomes another changing surface among the trees. Sargent's broad strokes do not isolate the tent as a rigid object set against the forest; they connect its light and shade with the surrounding ground. The open entrance makes its temporary shelter apparent. Habitation here depends on a thin, permeable boundary rather than on the weight of walls.

works.title: Incensing the Veil
works.credit: Τζον Σίνγκερ Σάρτζεντ. Incensing the Veil. Image credit: John Singer Sargent; Source credit: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: Hanging fabric, pale clothing and smoke interfere with a clear separation of figure and room. Sargent makes partial visibility the condition of the scene. Instead of searching for a single decisive outline, follow the layers through which the body becomes legible. The action named in the title affects how it can be seen: the incense also changes the air around it.

works.title: A Young Lady of Fashion
works.credit: Paolo Uccello. A Young Lady of Fashion. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The strict profile keeps the sitter's gaze outside any exchange with the viewer. Pearls and the patterned sleeve offer abundant information about her presentation, while the face remains bounded and reserved. Attributed to Paolo Uccello, the portrait gives social appearance an exact material form without claiming to reveal a private personality beneath it.

works.title: Morning Toilet
works.credit: Anders Zorn. Morning Toilet. Image credit: Anders Zorn; Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Anders_Zorn_-_Morning_Toilet_-_P25e13_-_Isabella_Stewart_Gardner_Museum.jpg. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Full-frame resize and JPEG compression; applicable ShareAlike terms retained.
works.description: The woman's bent posture keeps her activity readable amid the broken reflections. Zorn puts a private act beside shallow water and rocks, where the surrounding light refuses to remain still. The figure neither dominates the landscape nor disappears into it. Her small, concentrated movement supplies a point of attention within the more dispersed activity of the water.

closingSections.title: Let the room remain part of the work
paragraphs: The Gardner Museum's settings can affect a painting's scale and associations as strongly as a neighbouring picture. Give an arrangement time before isolating its individual objects. This selection follows themes rather than a physical route; use current museum information for access and display, and remember that works on paper may not be available continuously.
